extra.message: OS command injection on /ops/shell/course-probe-501/. The 'host' query parameter (line 145) is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system() ('ping -c 1 ' + host). An attacker can supply e.g. ?host=127.0.0.1;id or ?host=$(whoami) to execute arbitrary shell commands on the server. shlex quoting or subprocess with an argument list must be used instead of string concatenation into os.system().

extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) on /ops/jinja/course-cast-489/. The 'fragment' GET parameter (line 137) is concatenated into the Jinja2 template source string before Template() compiles and renders it. An attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions such as {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} to traverse Python object graphs and execute arbitrary code on the server. User input must never be embedded in template source; it should be passed as render context data.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: XML External Entity (XXE) injection on /ops/xml/course-fold-519/. The lxml parser is explicitly created with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False, then used to parse the raw request body via etree.fromstring(). External entity references are resolved, allowing an attacker to read local files (file:///etc/passwd), make server-side network requests (SSRF), and cause denial of service via entity expansion ('billion laughs'). The parser must disable DTD loading/external entity resolution (resolve_entities=False, load_dtd=False, no_network=True) or use defusedxml.

extra.message: Uploaded files are served without authentication when DEBUG is on (the default, see config/settings.py line 10). This completely bypasses the access control enforced by download_document() (lms/views.py:496-508), making student submission attachments, course resources, and feedback documents (PII) publicly downloadable at guessable paths such as /media/uploads/2026/09/<filename>. extra.message: Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY. When the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set, the application silently runs with the publicly-known key 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me'. If deployed this way, session cookies, signed cookies, password-reset tokens, and CSRF tokens are all signed with a known secret, allowing an attacker to forge sessions and bypass authentication. extra.message: CSV formula injection in the grade export (GET /reports/grades.csv). Student-controlled values set at self-registration (first_name/last_name via RegistrationForm, and email) and instructor-controlled assignment titles are written into CSV cells by csv.writer without neutralizing leading formula characters (=, +, -, @). When an instructor or admin opens grade_export.csv in Excel/LibreOffice/Google Sheets, a malicious value such as a first name of =HYPERLINK("http://evil/","x") or =cmd|'/c calc'!A0 is executed as a formula, enabling data exfiltration or command execution on the staff workstation. Cell values beginning with =, +, -, @, or tab should be prefixed with a single quote.

extra.message: File upload stores a client-controlled Content-Type without verification (also in upload_resource at lms/views.py:483). Document.content_type is populated from getattr(upload, 'content_type', ''), which is the MIME type asserted by the client's HTTP upload headers; no magic-byte or server-side content inspection is performed (only extension allowlisting for submissions). The stored, untrusted content type can drive content-type confusion in other code paths that rely on it for serving or filtering decisions.

extra.message: Unbounded query evaluation in export_grades(). The export iterates 'for sub in submissions:' over the full queryset with no row limit, pagination, or .iterator(), materializing every matching Submission (plus select_related rows) in memory. In contrast, sibling exports are capped (reports uses [:200], export_submissions_json uses [:500]). With a large submission table this allows an authenticated instructor/admin to trigger memory exhaustion and request timeouts (resource exhaustion).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Session and CSRF cookies lack the Secure attribute. The cookie configuration sets HttpOnly and SameSite but never sets SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE or CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE (and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT / SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS are absent). If the site is reachable over plain HTTP, the Django session cookie and CSRF cookie — which identify and authenticate the user — are transmitted unencrypted and can be captured by a network attacker. Both flags should be enabled so cookies are only sent over HTTPS.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Audit-log client IP is taken from the spoofable X-Forwarded-For header. client_ip() unconditionally prefers request.META['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR'] over REMOTE_ADDR, so every AuditLog.ip_address (written by audit() at lms/services.py:20) records whatever value the client chooses to send. Unless a trusted reverse proxy is guaranteed to overwrite this header, an attacker can forge the source IP recorded for their actions, defeating the integrity of the audit trail relied on for security review.

extra.message: API keys never expire. The APIKey model has no expires_at field or expiry logic, and api_course_assignments (lms/views.py:676) validates only token equality plus is_active=True. A leaked or forgotten API key therefore grants persistent read access to course assignment data indefinitely until manually deactivated. Security tokens should have a bounded lifetime with automatic expiry.
